title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
event_hint: arXiv research paper on fractal-based KV cache compression archive format
problem: KV cache dominates memory cost of long-context autoregressive inference; existing compression (quantization, eviction, offloading) addresses the lossy compression step, but the question of how to store the resulting symbol stream and whether the storage layer can enable retrieval and random access remains unaddressed.
mechanism: Contractive iterated-map codes (chaos game representation/universal sequence maps) serialize symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors, forming a lossless archive with O(1) random access, O(1) amortized append, linear-time encoding, and in-place substring search capability on stored vectors.

evidence.claim: Per-head residual VQ with hybrid bit allocation (K×4, V×2) achieves 36× compression vs fp16 at +11.2% perplexity cost
evidence.condition: GPT-2 124M, 1024-token context, 4-sink + 32-recent exact window, The Time Machine corpus

evidence.claim: Quantizing keys is ~4× more damaging to perplexity than quantizing values
evidence.baseline: values-only quantization (+4.0% perplexity) vs keys-only quantization (+14.5% perplexity)
evidence.condition: GPT-2, 1024-token context, per-head RVQ k=256×2 base configuration
evidence.source_locator: Table 2 and surrounding text, PDF Page 4

evidence.claim: Encoding performance: 0.68µs/char, 311µs random access lookup, 175µs/token append
Per-head codebooks Pareto-dominate pooled codebooks at equal bit budget
Archive supports approximate substring queries directly on stored vectors with full recall
evidence.baseline: sequential decoding required for arithmetic coding
evidence.condition: Stored vectors enable nearest-neighbor distance as graded suffix-similarity

evaluation_context: GPT-2 (124M parameters), The Time Machine corpus (public domain), 1024-token contexts, single laptop CPU, exact window = 4 attention sinks + 32 recent tokens (3.5% of context at 1024), perplexity as sole quality metric, exact baseline perplexity = 35.97, codebooks trained on disjoint span of same book via k-means
limitations: Small-scale study on single 124M-parameter model; only perplexity measured (no downstream task accuracy); per-head codebooks trained per-corpus not amortized; retrieval limited to suffix matching not semantic retrieval; serialization advantage is access pattern not compression ratio (uniform code 6.13 bits/char vs ~2.55 bits/char for order-2 model); larger models may tolerate more KV quantization but unvalidated
project_relevance: Relevant to cross-domain cache transfer as the fractal archive format provides: (1) high compression (36×) enabling lower bandwidth transfer of archived KV states; (2) O(1) random access enabling selective retrieval rather than full-cache transfer; (3) in-place search index for matching cached contexts; (4) linear-time encoding/decoding suitable for streaming transfers. The bit-asymmetric K/V quantization insight informs bandwidth-quality tradeoffs for cross-domain cache replication.
